title: Catering Marketing 101: Four Google Marketing Tools You Need to Master - Slamdot

facts.fact: The vendor states that 9 out of 10 people turn to Google when they need a local catering company.
facts.quote: 9 out of 10 people are going to turn to Google when they are in need of a local catering company.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a Google My Business profile can be set up for free.
facts.quote: Your catering business can set up a Google My Business profile for free.

facts.fact: The vendor describes Google Analytics as a free tool for monitoring, tracking and analyzing website traffic.
facts.quote: Google Analytics is a free tool that you can use to monitor, track and analyze all of your website traffic.

facts.fact: The vendor states that the Google Display Network includes millions of websites.
facts.quote: This includes millions of websites, from major media outlets to smaller niche-specific blogs.

facts.fact: The vendor states that Google Local Service Ads give the user two options: complete a request for more information or connect with the business immediately by phone.
facts.quote: the individual is given two options — complete a request for more information or connect with your business immediately on the phone.

facts.fact: The vendor states that Google Local Service Ads carry a Google Guaranteed program that guarantees the service up to the total cost.
facts.quote: a program that guarantees the service up to the total cost.

facts.fact: The vendor states that Google Local Service Ads are managed through an app for handling all calls and leads.
facts.quote: You field, respond to and manage all calls and leads from your Google local service ads through an app.

facts.fact: The vendor states that Google Maps local results appear right below paid ads and above organic results.
facts.quote: These are the prominent local search results that place local businesses on a map right below the paid ads and above the organic results.

facts.fact: The article was published on September 19, 2019.
